The retriever uses the DPR bi‑encoder to encode both the query and each document into dense vectors.  
It then performs a **Maximum Inner Product Search (MIPS)** over the document index: the top‑\(k\) documents whose vectors have the largest inner product with the query vector are returned as the retrieved set. This MIPS can be solved approximately in sub‑linear time.【rag-knowledge-intensive-nlp.pdf — Page 3】【rag-knowledge-intensive-nlp.pdf — Page 2】

claims.claim: The retriever uses the DPR bi-encoder to encode both the query and each document into dense vectors.
claims.evidence: The retrieval component pη(z|x) is based on DPR [26]. DPR follows a bi-encoder architecture: pη(z|x) ∝ exp(d(z)⊤q(x)) d(z) = BERTd(z), q(x) = BERTq(x) where d(z) is a dense representation of a document produced by a BERTBASE document encoder, and q(x) a query representation produced by a query encoder, also based on BERTBASE.

claims.claim: The retriever performs a Maximum Inner Product Search (MIPS) over the document index.
claims.evidence: Calculating top-k(pη(·|x)), the list of k documents z with highest prior probability pη(z|x), is a Maximum Inner Product Search (MIPS) problem
